British Aerospace 146: United Kingdom. Production figures include the Avro RJ, an improved version from Avro International Aerospace, a subsidiary of BAE Systems.
Who is credited with discovering Rutherfordium?
Rutherfordium: Albert Ghiorso. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Who is credited with discovering Ampère's force law?
Ampère's force law: André-Marie Ampère. In magnetostatics, Ampère's force law describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two current-carrying wires.
Who is credited with discovering Rhenium?
Rhenium: Walter Noddack. Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
This tsetse-fly-borne parasitic infection, caused by a protozoan, disproportionately affects humans and cattle across Africa — what is it?
Atrocities in the Congo Free State

African trypanosomiasis is an insect-borne parasitic infection of humans and other animals caused by the protozoan species Trypanosoma brucei, which is transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly.
This group of large, semiaquatic boas native to tropical South America includes the green species, among the largest snakes on Earth — name the group?
Anaconda are a group of large boas of the genus Eunectes.
Considered a visual art even though it leans on civil engineering, this discipline gives us cultural symbols that often outlast the civilizations that built them. What is it?
Architecture is the study and practice of designing structures, especially habitable ones.

Originating in Central Africa and classified as a hound by the American Kennel Club, this dog breed doesn't bark but instead makes an unusual yodel-like sound due to its uniquely shaped larynx — what's the breed?
Basenji is a breed of hunting dog created from stock that originated in Central Africa, including in the Republic of the Congo and other adjacent tropical African countries.
This small bird in the Old World flycatcher family breeds among rocky habitats from the British Isles to Morocco and east to central China — what species is it?
Black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family.

Forced to flee Italy in 1938 under the racial laws, this experimental physicist had earlier invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to show cosmic rays arrived more strongly from the West than the East — who was he?
Bruno Rossi (13 April 1905 - 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.

Honored twice by the American Psychological Association — in 1956 for scientific contributions and 1972 for professional ones — this psychologist championed a person-centered approach to therapy — who is he?
Carl Rogers (January 8, 1902 - February 4, 1987) was an American psychologist who was one of the founders of humanistic psychology and was known especially for his person-centered psychotherapy.
This plant-cell organelle uses chlorophyll pigments to capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy, ultimately producing sugar via the Calvin cycle — what is it?
Chloroplast (-plahst) is a type of organelle known as a plastid that conducts photosynthesis mostly in plant and algal cells.

Ranging across most of Europe and into the Palearctic as far as northwestern China, this medium-sized bird of prey sees its northernmost populations migrate as far as South Africa each winter — which raptor?
Common buzzard (Buteo buteo) is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range.

Caused by prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids like cortisol, this collection of symptoms includes abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and weak, fragile skin that heals poorly — what's it called?
Cushing's syndrome is a collection of signs and symptoms due to prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

This gut ailment flares up when small pouches in the wall of the large intestine become inflamed, often striking with sudden lower-abdominal pain — fever or bloody stool warns of a complication; what is it?
Diverticulitis is a gastrointestinal disease characterized by inflammation of abnormal pouches - diverticula - that can develop in the wall of the large intestine.
Many of these Northern Hemisphere shade trees, prized along old European and American streets, were wiped out by a fungus carried by bark beetles — which tree genus is this?
Elm are deciduous and semi-deciduous trees comprising the genus Ulmus in the family Ulmaceae.
First confirmed around a pulsar in 1992, this astronomical term describes any planet located outside our own solar system — over 6,300 have now been confirmed — what is it called?
Exoplanet is a planet outside the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.
This West Point graduate, eighth in his class of 670, commanded Apollo 8's historic flight around the Moon in 1968 — who is he?
Frank Borman (March 14, 1928 - November 7, 2023) was an American United States Air Force (USAF) colonel, aeronautical engineer, NASA astronaut, test pilot, and businessman.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-molecular-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione (GSH) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.

In 1896 this English physician dosed himself with mescaline and wrote one of the first public reports of the trip; he also co-wrote English's first medical textbook on homosexuality and coined the term 'narcissism' — who was he?
Havelock Ellis (2 February 1859 - 8 July 1939) was an English physician, eugenicist, writer, progressive intellectual and social reformer who studied human sexuality.
Found from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego across roughly 375 species, the males of this American bird family boast the most diverse plumage colors of any birds — what are they?
Hummingbird are birds native to the Americas and comprise the biological family Trochilidae.
An ISO standard defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — and it's related to, but not the same as, invention. What word are we after?
Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.
This psychologist edited 'Psychological Review' from 1910 to 1915 and was later ranked the 17th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century for popularizing behaviorism — who is he?
John B. Watson (January 9, 1878 - September 25, 1958) was an American psychologist who popularized the scientific theory of behaviorism, establishing it as a psychological school.
This unit of speed equals exactly one nautical mile per hour, roughly 1.15 mph, and is the standard measure used in maritime and aviation contexts — what is it called?
Knot (unit) is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, exactly 1.852 km/h (approximately 1.151 mph or 0.514 m/s).
Also called the great grey slug, this 10-20cm mollusc has a strange courtship where mating pairs suspend themselves in midair from a mucus thread — what species is it?
Limax maximus (literally, "biggest slug"), known by the common names great grey slug and leopard slug, is a species of slug in the family Limacidae, the keeled slugs.

Resembling some toxic look-alikes despite being a well-regarded edible, this basidiomycete fungus is a fairly common species on well-drained soils across temperate Eurasia, found solitary or in fairy rings in pastures — name the species?
Macrolepiota procera is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
First synthesized in 1982 near Darmstadt, this fleeting synthetic element of the periodic table's seventh period was named in 1997 after a pioneering Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist. What is it?
Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
This small, subterranean mammal has velvety fur, tiny eyes, and short powerful forelimbs with oversized paws built for constant digging — what animal is it?
In this category of over 80 recognized conditions, the body's adaptive immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissue as though it were foreign. What is it?

Navel (clinically known as the umbilicus; pl.: umbilici or umbilicuses; also known as the belly button or tummy button) is a protruding, flat, or hollowed area on the abdomen at the attachment site of the umbilical cord.
This insect order includes dragonflies and damselflies, the bulkier ones holding wings out at rest while the slender ones fold theirs along the body — what is it?
Odonata is an order of predatory flying insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies (as well as the Epiophlebia damsel-dragonflies).
Usually numbering four and tucked behind the thyroid, these small endocrine structures release a hormone that kicks in when blood calcium runs low — which structures?
Parathyroid gland are small endocrine glands in the neck of humans and other tetrapods.
What dissociative anesthetic, known on the street as a recreational drug, can cause hallucinations, paranoia, and psychotic behavior, and is often smoked or mixed with cannabis or tobacco?
Phencyclidine (PCP), also known in its use as a street drug as angel dust among other names, is a dissociative anesthetic mainly used recreationally for its significant mind-altering effects.
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it to the US in the 1820s, this red-and-green plant native to Mexico is a Christmas staple — what plant is it?
Poinsettia (Euphorbia pulcherrima) is a commercially important flowering plant species of the diverse spurge family Euphorbiaceae.
Split into roughly a dozen Afrotropical species and around 167 Neotropical species — among them the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which bird family is this?
Psittacidae is one of three families of true parrots.
What dimensionless quantity in fluid dynamics, expressing the ratio of inertial to viscous forces, determines whether a flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent?
Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity that helps predict fluid flow patterns in different situations by measuring the ratio between inertial and viscous forces.
Named after an American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, gram-negative bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes within a single major species — name it?
Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

This dog breed from southern China, traditionally kept as a property guardian, was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century and is known in the West for its deep wrinkles. What breed is this?

Shar Pei (Cantonese; pinyin: sh p) is a dog breed from
southern China.
This birth defect involves incomplete closure of the spinal column and its surrounding membranes during early pregnancy, occurring in three recognized forms — what condition is it?
Spina bifida (SB; Latin for 'split spine') is a birth defect in which there is incomplete closing of the spine and the membranes around the spinal cord during early development in pregnancy.
Named for its long, flat, sword-like bill, this large migratory predatory fish loses all its teeth and scales by adulthood and is a popular target among billfish anglers — what is it?
Swordfish (Xiphias gladius), also known as the broadbill in some countries, are large, highly migratory predatory fish characterized by a long, flat, sword-like, pointed bill.

This weakly radioactive silvery metal, atomic number 90, tarnishes olive-grey in air, and its most stable isotope has a half-life of about 14 billion years — roughly the age of the universe. What element is this?
Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
An important food fish found in marine and brackish waters from the Baltic to the Mediterranean, this flatfish's Black Sea relatives are now classified as a separate species — which fish?
Turbot is a relatively large species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
What's the name for the small, non-cancerous skin growths caused by the human papillomavirus, most common on the hands and feet but also appearing as genital or filiform forms?
Wart are non-cancerous viral growths usually occurring on the hands and feet but which can also affect other locations, such as the genitals or face.

This paraphilia describes a sexual fixation on non-human animals, distinct from acting on such attraction, and was estimated in one 2021 study to affect about 2 percent of the population — name the term?
Zoophilia is a paraphilia in which a person experiences a sexual fixation on non-human animals.
Regarded as one of Formula One's greatest engineers, his car designs have won 14 Drivers' and 12 Constructors' Championships across three decades?
Adrian Newey: British engineer, aerodynamicist and motorsport executive (born 1958)
This Swedish chemist held 355 patents, invented dynamite, and then left his fortune to fund a famous set of prizes. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel: Swedish chemist and inventor (1833–1896)

Inspired by Ørsted's 1820 discovery that current creates a magnetic field, this principle relating a magnetic field's circulation to the current passing through a loop was later generalized by Maxwell with a displacement current term — which physics principle?
Ampère's circuital law: Concept in classical electromagnetism.

A political economy professor turned finance minister after a 1926 coup, this Portuguese dictator ruled his corporatist 'New State' from 1932 until 1968, in one of modern Europe's longest authoritarian regimes — who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar: Prime Minister of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.

Also known by a folksy nickname, this small North American tree produces a custard-textured fruit tasting like banana or pineapple — despite containing a neurotoxin elsewhere in the plant. What species is it?
Asimina triloba: Species of tree. Asimina triloba, the American papaw, pawpaw, paw paw, or paw-paw, among many regional names, is a species of small deciduous tree.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?

Roughly a third of deaths from this group of over 100 diseases trace to tobacco, alcohol, obesity, poor diet and inactivity, and its malignant tumors are defined by uncontrolled cell growth that can spread — what is it?

Cancer: Group of diseases involving cell growth. Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
An obligate carnivore with retractable claws and crepuscular hunting habits, this small domesticated mammal communicates with everything from purrs and trills to hisses — what is it?
Cat: Small domesticated carnivorous mammal. The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
A political scientist studying voter turnout and race, this scholar rose through Harvard's deanships to become its 30th president in 2023 — only to resign months later; who is she?
Claudine Gay: American political scientist and university administrator (born 1970)

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
Carnivora splits into two suborders, dog-like and cat-like — which one groups cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids together?
Found at the end of the leg and typically featuring claws or nails, which weight-bearing body part enables locomotion in many vertebrates?
Foot: Anatomical structure found in vertebrates.

In 1974 in Pacific Grove, California, this computer scientist demoed the first working prototype of CP/M and invented the BIOS, then founded Digital Research to sell his software — who was this PC-revolution pioneer?
Gary Kildall: American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur (1942–1994)

Making up about 15% of all brain tumors and thought to arise from cells called astrocytes, this aggressive cancer often announces itself only with vague headaches or sudden personality changes — what is it?
Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Besides NASA, Roscosmos, ESA and JAXA, the fifth partner agency running the space station belongs to which country?
The Canadian Space Agency is the fifth partner. China is not a partner at all -- it built its own station, Tiangong.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.
This Berkeley professor gave us "fuzzy" everything — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control — proposing a whole branch of mathematics for reasoning with imprecision. Who was he?
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
A slender African cat with a tiny head and enormous ears, this golden, black-spotted hunter is the sole member of its genus and stands tall on remarkably long legs — which wild cat is it?
Known commonly as baking soda, this white crystalline compound with the formula NaHCO3 occurs naturally as the mineral nahcolite — what is its chemical name?
Sodium bicarbonate: Chemical compound. It is a salt composed of a sodium cation (Na+) and a bicarbonate anion (HCO−3).
A spherical, gram-positive bacterium that usually lives harmlessly on our skin and in our airways, this microbe can turn opportunistic and cause abscesses, sinusitis, and food poisoning — what is it?
Staphylococcus aureus: Species of Gram-positive bacterium. It is often positive for catalase and nitrate reduction and is a facultative anaerobe, meaning that it can grow without oxygen.
Among the largest flighted birds in their range, these waterfowl of genus Cygnus typically mate for life and lay three to eight eggs per clutch — what are they?
Swan: Tribe of large water birds.
In physics, temperature measures which property of a system's particles?
Temperature is an average, which is why a spark at 1000 degrees carries far less energy than a bathtub at 40 -- the bath has vastly more particles and so more total heat.
The largest cat of the genus Panthera, this Asian apex predator wears orange fur with mostly vertical black stripes and ranges from snowy Russian forests to tropical Indian jungles — what is it?
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
Used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder, this medication carries a serious risk of birth defects if taken during pregnancy — what is it?
Valproate: Medication used for epilepsy, bipolar disorder and migraine. Common side effects of valproate include nausea, vomiting, somnolence, and dry mouth.
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
This Japanese media artist and academic directs a research centre for 'Digital Nature' and holds visiting professorships at multiple Japanese art universities — who is he?
Yoichi Ochiai: Japanese academic, artist, and entrepreneur. Yoichi Ochiai (落合 陽一, Yoichi Ochiai; born 16 September 1987) is a Japanese media artist, entrepreneur, and academic.
What is the chemical symbol for tin?
The symbol for tin is Sn. Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn and atomic number 50.
What is the chemical symbol for copernicium?
The symbol for copernicium is Cn. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

Katharine Hepburn: Katharine Houghton Hepburn (May 12, 1907 – June 29, 2003) was an American actress whose career as a leading lady on stage and screen spanned six decades.

Walt Disney: Walter Elias Disney ( DIZ-nee; December 5, 1901 – December 15, 1966) was an American animator, film producer, voice actor, and entrepreneur.

John Candy: John Franklin Candy (October 31, 1950 – March 4, 1994) was a Canadian actor and comedian best known for his work in Hollywood comedy films.

Terrifier 2 is a 2022 American independent supernatural slasher film written, edited, co-produced, and directed by Damien Leone.
